title: Construction of a Preclinical Multimodality Phantom Using Tissue-mimicking Materials for Quality Assurance in Tumor Size Measurement
protocol: Cut all acrylic plates and rods required for silicone mold preparation with an accuracy of 25 μm.
Make five holes (diameter: 14, 10, 7, 4, 2 mm) for test objects in two acrylic base plates (size: 4.2 cm × 11.5 cm × 0.9 cm).
Cut spacer pairs with heights of 7, 5, 3.5, 2 and 1 mm (size: 1.0 cm × 5.5 cm).
Prepare steel balls (diameter: 14, 10, 7, 4 and 2 mm, accuracy: 2.5 μm).
Place two spacer pairs with a height of 7 mm and a base plate onto a thin acrylic plate in sequence.
Tighten the assembled components using C-clamps.
Insert the steel ball with a 14 mm diameter into the 14 mm hole of the base plate.
Glue the inserted steel ball using J-B KWIK.
Repeat the procedures for the remaining balls and the other base plate, ensuring that the steel balls in both plates are glued as mirror images.
Attach four acrylic plates, each 2.5 cm high with dimensions 2.5 cm × 11.5 cm or 2.5 cm × 4.2 cm, to one of the base plates using masking tape.
Attach a top plate (dimensions: 4.2 cm × 11.5 cm) to the base plate assembly, featuring five holes with 0.8 cm diameter and ten holes with 1.2 cm diameter.
Insert five acrylic rods (diameter: 0.8 cm, length: 0.5 cm) with 1 mm tips into the 0.8 cm holes of the top plate until they reach the top of the steel balls.
Glue the inserted acrylic rods using silicone glue.
Insert five alignment rods (diameter: 0.9 cm, length: 5.0 cm) through the larger holes in the top plate and into the base plate assembly.
Mix part A of the silicone rubber compound with part B at a ratio of 10 to 1 by weight.
Pour the mixed silicone rubber compound into the assembled structure.
Dry the assembly at room temperature for approximately 24 hours.
Screw the ground bolt to the end of the PVC pipe using a nut and a washer.
Pass commercial whole milk through 20 μm mesh filters.
Pass the filtered milk through 10 μm mesh filters.
Dissolve Thimerosal in the filtered milk.
Degas the Thimerosal-milk solution for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Dissolve dry agarose in deionized water.
Add 1-propanol and BaSO4 to the agarose solution.
Degas the agarose solution.
Heat the agarose solution in a 95 °C water bath until it clears.
Heat condensed milk in a 55 °C water bath.
Move the molten agarose solution to the 55 °C water bath to cool down.
Mix cooled agarose solution with heated condensed milk in a ratio of 1:1 by volume.
Slowly stir the mixture and remove air bubbles from the surface.
Add EDTA and CuCl2·2H2O to the agarose-milk mixture.
Stir sufficiently to ensure homogeneity.
Soak glass beads in concentrated nitric acid for 24 hours.
Rinse off the acid from the glass beads.
Pass commercial whole milk (20 cc) through a 20 μm mesh filter.
Pass the filtered milk through a 10 μm mesh filter.
Dissolve Thimerosal (0.02 g) in the filtered milk (10 cc).
Dissolve dry agarose (0.60 g) in deionized water (10 cc) and 1-propanol (0.79 cc).
Degas the agarose solution.
Heat the agarose solution in a 95 °C water bath until it clears.
Heat condensed milk in a 55 °C water bath.
Move the molten agarose solution to the 55 °C water bath.
Mix the heated agarose solution (5 cc) with the heated condensed milk (5 cc).
Slowly stir the mixture and remove air bubbles from the surface.
Add EDTA (0.0017 g) to the agarose-milk mixture.
Add CuCl2·2H2O (0.0010 g) to the agarose-milk mixture.
Stir sufficiently to mix all components thoroughly.
Attach nylon thread along the center of spheres on the silicone mold without 1 mm holes and glue it at both ends using silicone glue.
Apply silicone grease on the surface of two molds using a soft brush.
Assemble two molds using alignment rods.
Pour test object TM material through 1 mm holes of the silicone mold using a 22-gauge needle of a syringe.
Store the molds in a refrigerator (5 °C) for about 30 minutes to allow the test objects to set.
Make two holes of 1 mm at a depth of 10 mm from the phantom surface on each side of a half-cylindrical container for mounting nylon thread with test objects.
Make an additional hole of 6 mm in the half-cylindrical container to pour background TM material.
Unload the test objects with nylon thread from the molds.
Mount the test objects with nylon thread in the half-cylindrical container.
Adhere thin non-conducting aluminum (thickness: 0.12 mm) onto the acrylic container using 3M Scotch-Weld DP-100 and 3M duct tape.
Block the 1 mm holes in the acrylic container using 3M Scotch-Weld DP-100 glue.
Prepare background TM material quickly and pour it into the 6 mm hole of the container using a small plastic funnel.
Remove any air bubbles from the background TM material after pouring.
Glue the 6 mm hole using 3M Scotch-Weld DP-100 to seal it.
Rotate the phantom at 2 rpm in the rotator for 4 to 5 hours at room temperature.
Remove the nylon thread after the TM materials in the phantom completely hardens.
Scan the phantom in preclinical ultrasound.
Acquire images using CT scanning.
Obtain MRI images.
Follow imaging protocols described in Lee et al. for detailed procedures.
